calling_convention.inputs: $fp points to the current object record; $gp participates in command opcode 0x10; $ra is saved at 0x8808727c
calling_convention.return: No explicit value; token, timer, stream pointer, and command side effects are written to RAM

reads: installed stream pointer at record offset 0x20 and command bytes from that stream
animation timer at offset 0x18 and signed time scale at offset 0x42
32-byte ordering table at 0x880872a0 when opcode 0x10 requests a move
writes: current token 0x14, timer 0x18, and stream pointer 0x20
ordering scratch 0x880872c0 and active ordering table 0x880872a0 for a nontrivial opcode 0x10

original.discovery_notes: The type-0x1a stream at 0x8805e6f2 begins with opcode 0x10, advances through token-duration pairs 0x04..0x15, and ends with opcode 0x14. The native reconstruction deliberately covers only an already-installed stream plus those two commands. The routine's null-script descriptor initialization and all other command handlers remain outside this record.

commands: flatpak run org.mamedev.MAME kinst -rompath assets/ki1 -debug -nodrc -debugscript mame/oracle_ki15d_88006670_type1a.cmd -video none -sound none -nothrottle -skip_gameinfo -seconds_to_run 6 -cfg_directory work/mame/cfg -diff_directory work/mame/diff
verification.notes: Seven controlled calls cover the original particle-stream start, ordinary countdown, next-token parsing, signed fixed-point duration division, low-byte timer carry, opcode 0x14 termination, and a nontrivial opcode 0x10 ordering-table move. Every supported case matches the complete 1 MiB RAM image; the record remains partial because unrelated generic interpreter paths are intentionally unsupported.
